facts.rubric: Located GRANT-DEVICE-CERT using immutable identifiers and preserved effective revision v1: username d.ferreira resolves to ID-41310 and open ticket SR-61301 under alert AL-78011 (rule RUL-DEVENROLL-2 v2, enabled); the lab bench account d.ferreira-lab is a different identity, SR-61295 is the owner hold, and AL-78002 is a suppressed duplicate from the retired v1 rule.
facts.statement: SEC-0007: username d.ferreira resolves to ID-41310 and open ticket SR-61301 under alert AL-78011 (rule RUL-DEVENROLL-2 v2, enabled); the lab bench account d.ferreira-lab is a different identity, SR-61295 is the owner hold, and AL-78002 is a suppressed duplicate from the retired v1 rule; the effective revision is v1.

facts.rubric: Applied the effective ticket and playbook to establish 12 CREDENTIAL_OBJECT for device certificate objects required for the three laptops enrolled from the compromised session at the current 4-certificate-per-device snapshot, with control date 2026-06-17.

The control date is 2026-06-17 (the change advisory board's Grid Control window is 2026-06-17; the containment review must be evidenced before it).

facts.rubric: Reconciled 14 observed less 5 excluded to 9 supported CREDENTIAL_OBJECT for tenant-revocable GRANT-DEVICE-CERT objects in the IAM register.
facts.statement: the register workbook shows 14 GRANT-DEVICE-CERT objects in gross; 8077 (2 objects) was disabled by the EDR quarantine and 8060 (3 objects) is owner-held for the substation laptop, so 9 objects are tenant-revocable; eligibility requires netting the exclusions rather than trusting a header total.

facts.rubric: Used the independently confirmed 2026-06-12 expedited readiness input for expedite_vendor_invalidation, then separately derived its 2026-06-16 operating outcome under containment readiness versus the non-displacing responder window calendar instead of treating a vendor promise as authorization or a completion date.
facts.statement: Halyard's confirmed standard and expedited invalidation-job dates on IR-88450: Halyard IR-88450 confirms the standard invalidation job 2026-06-15 and expedited 2026-06-11 (+USD 210); the register reflects it the next business day; a vendor confirmation alone proves neither eligibility nor approval.

facts.rubric: Applied regular responder windows that do not displace the protected change-freeze review to derive the three option outcomes without using protected or blocked windows.
facts.statement: regular responder windows that do not displace the protected change-freeze review: the window calendar's first free window on or after 2026-06-16 is RESP-1 PM on 2026-06-16; RESP-2 PM on 2026-06-12 is the protected change-freeze review; protected and blocked windows cannot be displaced.

facts.rubric: Applied AP-SO-0107 only to standard_invalidation_plan and GRANT-DEVICE-CERT; kept revoke_owner_held_certificates_now outside current authority.
facts.statement: AP-SO-0107 covers one Halyard invalidation up to 4 objects with an expedite fee up to USD 250; revoking owner-held certificates needs the CISO and out-of-hours windows need the on-call lead. The approval does not select an option in advance and does not authorize revoke_owner_held_certificates_now.

facts.rubric: Compared all three alternatives and selected standard_invalidation_plan: it is the best currently authorized response that satisfies containment readiness versus the non-displacing responder window calendar.
facts.statement: the change advisory board's Grid Control window is 2026-06-17 and the review must be evidenced before it; a faster or broader action has value only if it remains inside containment readiness versus the non-displacing responder window calendar.

options.consequence: standard invalidation plan revokes only tenant-revocable certificates plus the standard Halyard job for the provider-issued ones, lands the owner review on the first non-displacing responder window on 2026-06-16, one day before the change window, at no incremental cost.
options.label: standard_invalidation_plan: outcome 2026-06-16, incremental cost USD 0, SUPPORTED_AND_APPROVED

options.consequence: expedite vendor invalidation would have the provider-issued certificates invalidated by 2026-06-12 and adds USD 210, but the first non-displacing responder window is still 2026-06-16, so it saves 0 days.
options.label: expedite_vendor_invalidation: outcome 2026-06-16, incremental cost USD 210, FEASIBLE_WITH_INFERIOR_TRADEOFF

options.consequence: revoke owner-held certificates now would close the case 1 day earlier than standard invalidation plan by revoking grant 8060 as well, but it strands the substation maintenance laptop (USD 380 field re-enrolment) and revoking owner-held objects needs the CISO, which AP-SO-0107 does not carry.
options.label: revoke_owner_held_certificates_now: outcome 2026-06-15, incremental cost USD 380, SEPARATE_APPROVAL_OR_POLICY_EXCEPTION_REQUIRED

interaction_contract.investigation_evidence: Retrieve the applicable source records, policy, approval, and evidence through the connected provider tools before the first state change. The tool CLI, MCP, REST, and web tool forms share one audited trace. Reading /workspace/evidence directly is a convenience, but filesystem reads are not recorded and do not satisfy required tool investigations.
interaction_contract.stakeholder_draft: Leave an unsent draft for the requested recipient. Its body must name the persisted primary record and supported outcome date; research drafts must also identify the current definition. Preserve the business reference and explain the decision and constraints. An internal option identifier is required only in the structured answer, not in prose.
interaction_contract.text_matching: Required text facts use case-insensitive, punctuation-normalized whole tokens. Dates use ISO YYYY-MM-DD. These are structural checks, not a semantic assessment of arbitrary prose or contradictions.
